A1.justification: Despite the changed title and format, both PDFs describe the same Cluster-DP research. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing relocated material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 Section 5 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations and simulations using YouTube communities, including variance, conditional-bias, and Gaussianity results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results in Section 4 and Appendices A.6–A.10, including the simulations using YouTube communities.

M1.justification: v2 Algorithm 4 and v3 Algorithm 2 retain the same Laplace perturbation, clipping, renormalization, and response-resampling procedure. The inverse-Q estimator and the mechanism's special cases are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Gaussian-mixture simulations and the same semi-synthetic YouTube setting: 50 communities containing 22,179 users with simulated potential outcomes. Appendix relocation introduces no additional dataset, task, or test scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Cluster-Free-DP, stratified and unstratified Uniform-Prior-DP, and the non-private reference. The one-shot comparison retains noisy Horvitz–Thompson and noisy histogram estimators. Newly discussed related papers do not add evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Cluster sizes, balanced treatment assignments, outcome quantization, privacy targets, and parameter-search grids match. YouTube preprocessing and experimental parameters also remain unchanged; the appendix experiments reproduce existing protocols.

E4.justification: Both retain cluster-quality sensitivity, bias and Gaussianity checks, theoretical variance-bound validation, and the one-shot conditional-bias analysis. Several analyses move from v2 Section 5 to v3 Appendices A.6–A.9 without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Both retain 500 simulation realizations and the same error-bar procedures, including 50 independent subpopulation draws for the trade-off experiment. The one-shot analysis still uses 500 subpopulations and 50 privacy-mechanism realizations.

E6.justification: The experimental plots retain identical curves, points, and error bars, and the reported findings match. v2 Figures 4–6 and 10 become panels in v3 Figures 2 and 8; the remaining results are retained under new locations and numbering.

T1.justification: v3 requires at least two units per cluster, replacing v2's explicit allowance of singletons. Appendix A.13 also replaces an asserted equivalence in the privacy proof with a sufficient inequality respecting the positive-part definition of delta. The principal privacy and variance bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the claimed applicability from unrestricted cluster sizes, including singletons, to clusters containing at least two units. The central claims about improving the privacy–variance trade-off and generalizing the baseline mechanisms remain intact.

C2.justification: v3 adds discussion distinguishing label-DP protection from inference through feature–label correlations. New Remark 3.3 interprets the existing spectral bound as a conditioning guarantee. The previous cluster-quality interpretation and aggregation-baseline limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Remark 3.3 adds parameter-selection advice, specifically sigma < epsilon, for the claimed conditioning of Q. The inverse formula and spectral bound already appeared in v2's appendix. Experimental settings and dataset-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 substantially revises research positioning: it adds Guha and Reiter (2024), Lee et al. (2019), and Ohnishi and Awan (2023), while removing several broader background references. It also considerably expands the comparison with Esfandiari et al. (2022), addressing assumptions, cluster homogeneity, and the distinct variance analysis.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title, extensively revises the opening narrative and related work, combines the problem setup with a baseline overview, and reorganizes detailed baselines and experiments into the appendix. It adds a conclusion and impact statement, but also leaves template instructions at the appendix's end.

P2.justification: The main text changes to a two-column conference layout. Four separate plots become a compact Figure 2 and a larger appendix Figure 8; other figures and algorithms move, and the notation glossary becomes tabular. The underlying scientific graphics are reused.

improvement.justification: The cluster-size qualification, refined privacy-proof step, and expanded research positioning improve precision and exposition. However, new Remark 3.3 overstates conditioning from lambda < 1 and gives sigma < epsilon advice unsupported by the displayed privacy bound. Small main-text plots, stale cross-references, and leftover template prose also reduce polish. With unchanged methods and empirical evidence, these competing corrections and new defects leave the net quality direction unclear.
